Yeah.
Yeah.

Definitely.

So we are a capital A.

Yep.

And we've.

So they're very much in the immersive experiential space.
So immersive creative companies.

So.
Okay.
So, yeah.
And they're very interested in your company too.
Smooth technology.

For sure there's an alignment.
Yeah, for sure.
You know, it's something that like has come up a few times in our history.

Yeah.
Cool.
So these guys, they basically are private investors.
Their background is more on the cloud computing side of things.
But they're kind of.
At least one of them is very much a technologist, I would say.
Okay.
But they built and sold companies within the cloud computing space.
Many, they are now of the mind that spatial computing is the future.
Yeah.
And they very much see the same pattern happening as they did in the, the sort of mid to late 90s with the Internet and the cloud computer space they're from.
So that's kind of background very much from the enterprise sort of side of things.
So they're, they're kind of used to finding businesses, scaling them, and then exiting to.
To one of the number one, two or three sort of leading businesses in the, in those spaces.

And very much this is the plan to acquire a bunch of companies who are at the cutting edge of spatial computing, build a business that's worth 100 million plus and exit to the number one or two or three in the next three to five years.
We're already about a year or so in to that plan.
Cool, that's great.
I mean, we're aligned for sure in the terms of where experiential meets spatial computing.
We've been at the forefront of that for a while and we're seeing this wave that I'm sure they're seeing as well, which is of social gaming spaces, more nuanced interactive spaces.
So more than just a kind of a children's museum where there's interactive moments, the entire experience is tracked based in the cloud.
And we just opened a business called Game Grounds in Ohio that is capitalizing on that.
And it's.
It's not a.

We're one of the smaller players in it, but we're looking at everyone else and how much money is being put into it.
And it seems like we're kind of not alone in thinking that that's going to be a really valuable industry.
Yeah, brilliant.
Perfect.
Well, that's great that you're kind of aligned and you're thinking around the same kind of thing.
Just for this.
This meeting I want to set up with my client, I just.
Obviously I've got some kind of not personal questions, but business questions, that if we can go into that.
That meeting with them already prepped, and they can kind of get you as down as possible, you know, with what that's going to look like.
So if you don't mind me asking just some questions about the business.
Who.
Who is the.
The owner and sort of shareholders of the business that you have?
Is it all you, David?
I'm one of them.
Yeah, we are.

Okay.
And how's that shareholding split?
Mostly.
It's mostly even.
Okay, so sort of 25% each, roughly.
And who was the founder of the business?
Did you all come together at the same time?
Three out of the four of us did, yeah.
Is there a sort of leader of the business, or do you all have, like, a fair.
That would be me.
Me, day to day.
Although we generally share decision making.
But day to day, I'd say if there is one person, it's me.
Is everybody of the same mind as you?
You know, obviously you sound quite keen, but is everybody thinking the same way?
Yeah, we are.
I think we all, you know, we would all make, you know, we've heard good stories and bad stories about companies in our position that have, you know, that have made that choice.
So I think we're all cautiously optimistic.
Yeah, I would say is the way to put it.
Yeah.
Good place to be.
The office that you've got in Dumbo, is that the only office that you have?
We have one in Ohio and one in Providence, Rhode Island.
But this is our.
This is the largest.
Okay.
And how many people in each office is.
Here's about six.
And in Rhode Island's one to two.
Ohio is one.
What's the reason for all those offices?
Just because two of our partners moved out of.
Outside of New York City.

And on Providence is generally where we make our heavy duty Electronics, our circuit boards and stuff.
And so that's a small team there.
Have you got a workshop there?
Yep, we do.
Cool.
And those offices, are they all rented?
One.
The one in Providence, is rented.
The one in Ohio is part of our partner's house, so.
And the one in Dumbo is rented.
Rented, Yep.
Okay.
So no real estate involved.
In terms of the rest of the team, is that everybody, or is there more freelancers or permanent.
It is mostly freelancers.
Beyond that, what roughly would you say the headcount is at the moment?
Right now?
It's.
I'd say nine.
Okay.
Okay.
So in terms of, like, the business development and the clients, who.
Who owns those relationships?
Is that you, David?
For the most part.
Two of my other partners have managed some of those relationships, but it's mostly me.
And do you do.
Are you sort of active with Biz Devil, or do you kind of just have people knocking on the door to work with you?
Traditionally, we just have not done outreach.
We decided after Covid to start doing that, and so we do outreach.
It's usually through creative pursuits, so doing projects that have high visibility, doing projects for ourselves.
Like, we're working on one now, releasing things that are just intended to show us as leaders in the field.
And then I do a lot of public speaking in the world of art and tech and academia, and so that we end up meeting a lot of folks in the live production, advertising space through those.
Okay, brilliant.
So given that it's mostly the founders, I guess, that are kind of working together, what would you say the culture of the business is?
Is there a way to sort of define it or.
Yeah, I think it's.
You know, it's a.
It's based around doing things that bring people joy.
And we try to make sure that, like, the experience of working here is positive.
And I think that that has been successful.
I was a high school teacher for a long time, and so I play a role, sort of mentor, like, role to a lot of our employees as they come up through our company.
And so that's a big part of it, where we have, like, we bring people in who kind of show promise in the younger sort of employees and help them learn how to, you know, get better.
And I think that that's appreciated.
When he needs employees.
Do you mean the freelancers?
Yeah, and they're sort of like, go from being almost full time to being part time based on the work that we've got, but we have a pretty regular relationship with them.
So I would say it's.
It's.
They Technically are freelancers, but they're part of a company called Trick, for sure.
Okay, so in terms of like the.
The sort of clients that you do get, what does.
What does sort of the typical client look like on typical project?
Is there like sort of a sweet spot that you guys shoot for or do you just kind of the best.
Yeah, in the world of advertising, it's like projects that are for large advertising agencies, large brands and building stuff.
And the jobs are usually somewhere between like 75 and 300k, probably a good, good, like reference point.
And then do you normally work to.
The ad agencies or do you do brand.
Mostly the ad agencies, but we have a few brands we work directly with, which is obviously preferable.
Yeah.
Okay, cool.
And then in terms of like, sort of the annual revenue, how much?
I mean, just sort of ballpark figures.
Yeah, sure.
Maybe like varying from 1 to 2 million.
Okay, was.
Is it going up or down?
Is it.
Oh, it's currently going up.
No, it's simply.
No, I think that since COVID it's been going up.
It was going up before COVID And the industry itself, we've seen change quite a bit, and we've seen a lot of companies our size and in our industry struggling.
And so we've seen that certainly are sort of growth slow last year and then pick up again luckily this year.
So you're sort of heading towards 2 million revenue for this?
Yeah.
Yes.
And what would you say last year was something like one and a half or something like that?
Something between.
Yeah, between one and one and a half.
Yeah.
Okay.
And profitable business is profitable?
Yes.
Yeah, it's profitable and our overhead's pretty low.
What would you say the margin is?
Do you know roughly what it is?
I would have to talk to my partner, James, who does the books about that, to give you a better number, but I can.
I can talk to him and get back to you.
Okay.
All right.
Yeah.

Because the way that, I mean, I'm sure you know this already, businesses, service businesses in the sort of marketing sector are always valued by multiples of ebitda, which is basically your profits before taxes and interest and all that sort.
So, yeah, I mean, if you could get us that number, that will give us a really clear picture on what likely from a financial perspective the offer would look like.
For sure be kind of good, sort of.
I mean, you sound like you're very positive around the whole idea of working within a larger business and maybe going through the process of being acquired.
But do you guys.
Are you working towards anything like an Exit or is it just passive interest?
Well, currently our, you know, our model of moving towards equity in businesses that use our technology is something that we're doing now for the first time successfully.
And I think that for us, that's a path to being able to build stuff that creates its own passive income while we are getting to do creative work, which is really what we're passionate about.

And I think that that would be our version of an exit, essentially, like building up, building up equity in businesses that are bringing us profit, like the social gaming space type businesses, and then being able to continue to work creatively with artists, performing artists, things like that.
So we do really enjoy that.
That's kind of like what we, what we like.
You know, if that looked like selling a business and then starting another to do that stuff, we'd be open to that.
Yeah.
So, well, how it would most likely work would be there would be cash up front, which would be roughly sort of half, 40%, 50%.
There'll be some equity rollover into the holding company.
But the idea really would be to build towards an exit for everybody.
Sure.

And like I say, they're looking for quite a large exit for the whole, for the whole group, but it's still early days, so, you know, they're very keen for founders like yourselves to stay in the business for that period.
And there's still obviously space on the, on the bench, you know, for people to come in as it's, it's fairly early.
So would you say everybody is keen to stick around over the next couple of years if they were to be acquired?
Or are the people that are looking to get out?
No, I think, I think we need to really.
I mean, if you think about our value, a lot of it is in our ip, but then a lot of it is in our actual people.
And I think that probably for it to be successful, we'd want to do that because we would want to leave it in a place where it's really good.
So I think we all believe in it and would.
Would want that.
Yeah.
Okay, brilliant.
All right, cool.
So next steps really is just to.
Is to get this meeting set up.
So just really need availability.
Who.
Who would you say needs to be on that call with you?
Is it just you at this stage?
I can talk to my partners.
I bet one other makes.
Probably makes sense for one other partner to join.
Okay.
So it's not just being by myself.
Yeah, yeah, yeah.
Well, there's probably going to be a lot of questions.

Yeah, any questions?
And then really these guys are quite quick movers as well.
So if we get the financials from you soon after that, if you're still interested, then they do tend to put offers in very, very quickly.
So, um, yeah, I don't know how ready you guys are, but could be a.
Could be a.
A very quick.
Could be a roller coaster.
Okay, cool.
We're.
We're used to quick deadlines.
Yeah, good, good.
Cool.
Um, so I'll get that to you for sure.

Well, I mean, they're kind of based in the other to some degree.
So Jeff is kind of the.
The.

Okay, that's fantastic.
David.
Thank you for being so open.
For sure.

We'll get some times.
Agreed.

All right, brilliant.
Thank you.
Sounds great.

Perfect.
Perfect.
Okay.
Yeah, Fantastic.
Okay.

Thanks like guys.
